title: RaCo GridSample WebGPU rewrite measurement
scope: Incremental comparison against the already SELU-decomposed RaCo graph; four synthetic DIC pairs, including 60% tensile stress.

hardware.adapter: <GPUAdapterInfo dict with vendor='Intel open-source Mesa driver', architecture='', device='Intel(R) Graphics (LNL)', description='Mesa 25.2.8-0ubuntu0.24.04.4', stackgroup_min_size=4, stackgroup_max_size=128, vendor_id=32902, device_id=25760, adapter_type='IntegratedGPU', backend_type='Vulkan'>
hardware.runtime: ONNX Runtime 1.31.1 with native WebGPU EP 0.5.0

input.timing: median of ONNX inference plus GPU local affine fit; image decoding and resizing excluded

rewrites: 83 Selu nodes decomposed to WebGPU-supported primitive operators, same pre-existing baseline used for both timing runs
37 zero-padded bilinear GridSample nodes rewritten as coordinate/weight operations plus GatherND(batch_dims=1)

interpretation: The trace contains provider event times and copy estimates, not hardware GPU timestamp queries or measured bus bandwidth.
MemcpyToHost and MemcpyFromHost byte sums are ORT trace estimates and can count repeated tensors.
CPU provider event count increases because the rewrite expands one GridSample into many primitive graph nodes, while summed CPU operator time and the large host transfer volume decrease.

rejected_logsoftmax_followup.reason: Rejected: although the diagnostic estimated D2H volume fell further, three-repeat production latency regressed versus GatherND-only in all four cases.
rejected_logsoftmax_followup.caveat: The profile establishes provider placement, but the added launch and synchronization cost is not isolated as a direct causal measurement.

limitations: The model's global inference still runs at 640x360, not native 4K; these measurements are not the native-4K refinement pipeline.
The ONNX Runtime WebGPU provider still has CPU fallbacks, including Expand and two border-padded GridSample nodes.
ONNX Runtime and wgpu-py do not share a demonstrated GPU allocation; final RANSAC still consumes returned matches through the current API.
No GPU peak-allocation measurement was available.
